recommended.title: Recommended vaccines
recommended.subtitle: For travel up to 6 months

items.title: Hepatitis B
items.text: Hepatitis B is a viral infection caused by a viral infection - potentially serious and chronic. Hepatitis B is widespread in large parts of the world.

items.title: Hepatitis A
items.text: Hepatitis A, also called contagious hepatitis, is an acute infectious liver disease caused by a virus. Vaccination against hepatitis A is not part of the national vaccination program.

items.title: Diphtheria
items.text: Diphtheria is a bacterial infection. Toxins produced by the bacterium can damage the nerves and the heart muscle. Combination vaccinations, which also work against diphtheria, are part of the national childhood vaccination program.

items.title: Yellow fever
items.text: Yellow fever is an acute viral disease transmitted by mosquito bites, which can lead to hemorrhagic fever and death. Vaccination is not part of the national vaccination program.

items.title: Malaria
items.text: A serious, even life-threatening febrile illness, caused by malaria parasites and spread by mosquitoes. Preventive treatment with malaria medicine can be used

items.title: Rabies
items.text: A viral disease which affects the central nervous system and ultimately causes encephalitis and death. Rabies is transmitted through the saliva of an infected animal. Vaccination against rabies is not part of the national childhood vaccination program.

items.title: Tetanus
items.text: A disease caused by an infection with a bacterium normally found in soil. Combination vaccination, which also applies to tetanus, is part of the national childhood vaccination program.

items.title: Tuberculosis
items.text: A contagious and potentially fatal bacterial disease that is widespread throughout the world.

items.title: Typhoid fever
items.text: Typhoid fever is a serious bacterial infection transmitted through contaminated food and water. Vaccination against typhoid is not part of national vaccination programs in most countries.

about.title: Algeria
about.text: In the largest country in Africa, you can experience the warm, sand-filled scirocco wind in the summer. The majority of the country is made up of the almost uninhabited Sahara desert.
about.textTwo: Sometimes called Algiers the White, the capitals bustling showpiece is its UNESCO-listed Casbah. This whitewashed medina encompasses both crumbling ruins and newly-renovated spaces and is well worth a visit despite its shady reputation (taking a guide is recommended).
about.notice: The vaccines listed for Algeria are the general recommendations of the health authorities. At the vaccination, a specific recommendation is given based on an assessment of the traveler's specific situation (s). This may deviate from the general recommendations.
